title: When Code Becomes an LLM Call: An Empirical Study of Call-Site Contracts in Agentic Systems
title_zh: 【当代码变成一次LLM调用：智能体系统中调用点契约的实证研究】

paragraphs.en: 该研究分析40个开源智能体系统中496个LLM调用点的契约落实情况，发现多数约束未被满足，存在系统性风险。 Software quality has long rested on specifications that state what code must do, and on testing and verification that check that the code does it. Agentic systems change this foundation: they replace parts of their logic, such as choosing the next tool, judging whether an action is allowed, or writing code to run, with calls to a large language model (LLM). The program still relies on what this logic must guarantee, but the model's behavior is not fixed by code, varies across runs, and can be steered by its input. The guarantee must therefore come from the program around each LLM call site, as a contract of pre-conditions, prompt constraints, and post-conditions. We present an empirical study of these contracts in 496 LLM call sites of 40 popular open-source agentic systems (13.4 MLOC, four languages). Using a multi-agent pipeline validated by 17,428 human judgments, we trace where every model output flows, derive an expected contract for each call site without access to its code, and compare it with the contract that the code implements. We find that 48% of LLM outputs reach control flow or execution, and 73% of these never reach a person. Programs enforce 78% of their constraints in code, but in the prompt, 67% of the constraints are only requested from the model. Although 82% of call sites are checked before and after the call, 63% of the expected constraints are unmet and only 5.3% of call sites satisfy their whole contract; ten recurring patterns explain 99% of the gaps. 38 mechanisms behind these gaps trigger at runtime, and a small code fix that enforces the expected constraint stops all 38. Our results show that the presence of checks says little about their adequacy, and we derive implications for agent developers, framework maintainers, and researchers.
paragraphs.zh: 软件质量长期以来依赖于说明代码必须做什么的规格说明，以及验证代码确实这样做了的测试与验证。该研究分析40个开源智能体系统中496个LLM调用点的契约落实情况，发现多数约束未被满足，存在系统性风险。 智能体系统改变了这一基础：它们将部分逻辑——例如选择下一个工具、判断某个动作是否被允许、或编写待运行的代码——替换为对大语言模型（LLM）的调用。 程序仍然依赖这些逻辑必须保证的内容，但模型的行为并不由代码固定，会随运行而变化，并且可以被其输入所左右。 因此，这种保证必须来自每个LLM调用点周围的程序，表现为由前置条件、提示词约束和后置条件构成的契约。 我们对40个流行的开源智能体系统（1340万行代码，四种语言）中496个LLM调用点的这些契约进行了实证研究。 利用一个经17,428条人工判断验证的多智能体流水线，我们追踪每个模型输出的流向，在不接触其代码的情况下为每个调用点推导出期望契约，并将其与代码实际实现的契约进行比较。 我们发现，48%的LLM输出会进入控制流或执行过程，而其中73%的输出从未到达人工环节。 程序在代码中落实了78%的约束，但在提示词中，67%的约束只是向模型提出请求而已。 尽管82%的调用点在调用前后都有检查，但63%的期望约束未被满足，且仅有5.3%的调用点满足其完整契约；十个反复出现的模式解释了99%的差距。这些差距背后的38种机制会在运行时触发，而一个落实期望约束的小型代码修复即可阻止全部38种。 我们的结果表明，检查的存在与否并不能说明其是否充分，并且我们为智能体开发者、框架维护者和研究者推导出了相关启示。
